summary: Theme-switcher fix is WORKING on web. Key metrics T2 (Light) and T3 (Dark) both PASS — palette now swaps correctly after window.location.reload() because src/theme/index.ts reads localStorage synchronously at module load. Persistence (T5), System-mode media tracking (T4/T4b with CDP emulation), and no-reload-loop (T6, nav_count=2) also pass. Only residual issue: when no pref exists (T1 fresh / T7 cleared storage), the Theme row label shows 'Dark (Material You)' (because getTheme() default is 'dark') while the resolved palette is light-media (because readSyncPref returns null for missing key and the resolver falls through to Appearance.getColorScheme() which returns 'light' in a light-mode browser). The review request stated this case should 'render in dark (fallback)', but the fix implementation prefers Appearance over a hard-coded dark default. This creates a cosmetic label/palette disagreement on first launch only; once the user picks any explicit mode, label and palette stay in sync. No console errors.

ui_bugs.issue: On first launch (no 'prefs.theme' in localStorage) the Theme row label shows 'Dark (Material You)' (settings.ts getTheme default='dark') while the palette renders Light because resolveScheme falls through to Appearance.getColorScheme() which reflects the browser prefers-color-scheme (light on default Chromium). Expected by review: fallback dark. Either (a) hard-fallback to 'dark' when readSyncPref() returns null AND no explicit pref exists, OR (b) change the row label to also respect Appearance when pref is unset. Low priority — self-heals once user makes a choice. Reference: /app/frontend/src/theme/index.ts:117-121, /app/frontend/src/utils/settings.ts:26-29.

rca_of_issue: Residual-only (low priority). On first launch no 'prefs.theme' is stored, so readSyncPref() returns null and resolveScheme() falls through to Appearance.getColorScheme(). On RN-Web, Appearance.getColorScheme() reads window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'). In a default Chromium viewport the media query returns 'light', so the palette resolves to LIGHT. Meanwhile the ThemeRow renders using themeMode state loaded via getTheme() which hard-defaults to 'dark' (settings.ts:27). Hence the row says 'Dark' while the UI is Light. FIX OPTIONS: (1) In src/theme/index.ts: return 'dark' as the ultimate fallback instead of Appearance.getColorScheme() when pref is truly null (matches review's stated expectation but loses OS-tracking on first launch). (2) In src/utils/settings.ts: change getTheme default to 'system' so the row label matches when no explicit choice exists. (3) Leave as-is since any explicit user action immediately resolves the discrepancy. Option (2) is the cleanest — makes 'first launch' == 'system mode' which is also the modern mobile convention.

Recommend (b) — it's one line and aligns label with Appearance-based palette.
